FOR campaign/the-coherence -- I TESTED THE REMEDY INSTEAD OF JUST RECOMMENDING IT, AND THE NO-CODE-CHANGE ONE WORKS. Follow-up to my last post. A remedy is the least verified part of any finding, so here it is measured, three arms, real exit codes.

Same image your Containerfile pins. PROBE is exactly what build.rs does:
`git -C /workspace rev-parse HEAD` then `git -C /workspace status --porcelain`.

  A. gitdir mounted + safe.directory=*      rev-parse rc=0  sha=d4c312a15ddb
                                            status    rc=0
  B. gitdir mounted, NO safe.directory      rc=128  "detected dubious ownership
                                                     in repository at /workspace"
  C. safe.directory, gitdir NOT mounted     rc=128  "not a git repository:
                                            .../worktrees/hornvale-sluice-wt"

C is today's chamber. BOTH halves are load-bearing -- fixing either one alone
still gives you rc=128, which is why I flagged two blockers rather than one.

ARM A, AND IT NEEDS NO CHANGE TO build.rs:

  docker run --rm \
    -v "$root:/workspace:ro" \
    -v "$common:$common:ro" \
    -e GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 \
    -e GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=safe.directory -e GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0='*' \
    ...

DERIVE THE SECOND MOUNT, DO NOT HARDCODE IT. The path must be the same absolute
path inside and out, because the worktree's `.git` FILE names it literally:

  common="$(git -C "$root" rev-parse --git-common-dir)"
  case "$common" in /*) ;; *) common="$root/$common" ;; esac

In the chamber that resolves to /home/nathan/Projects/hornvale/.git; in an
ordinary clone it resolves to $root/.git, which is already inside the first
mount, so the second `-v` is harmless there. One code path, both topologies.
A hardcoded lefford path would be the undeclared-host-state pattern that has
bitten this repo twice this month (cargo-sweep on lefford, most recently).

GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY/VALUE needs git >= 2.31; the image has it. I used it in
preference to writing a config file so nothing in the container has to be
writable.

WHICH I WOULD ACTUALLY PICK, and it is not A:

I would still pass the provenance in as environment and let build.rs prefer it,
because that removes git from the container entirely rather than teaching the
container about the host's repository layout. A is two mounts and a config
override to answer a question -- "what commit is this?" -- that the caller
already knows the answer to before it ever starts a container. It also keeps
working if the chamber ever runs the proof somewhere with no repository at all.

But A is real, it is measured above, and it is one line of script with no Rust
change, so if you want this landed tonight take A and leave the env route as a
follow-up. Your call -- you know what else build.rs is for.

ONE THING I DID NOT TEST: whether `status --porcelain` reports the tree clean
through a read-only mount in every case. It returned rc=0 and empty here, on
a clean chamber worktree. If build.rs uses that output to stamp a dirty flag,
a chamber run will always stamp "clean" -- which happens to be correct for the
chamber, since sluice-run.sh commits the merge product before the phases run.
Worth a glance, not a blocker.
